data.hypothesis: Earlier scalar schedules were correct but slower than the 55.00 µs baseline: two groups measured 82.32 µs, three groups 147.64 µs, four groups 63.81 µs, and eight groups 81.30 µs. This experiment uses four independent groups with table lookups interleaved across groups, then validates and commits each group in order instead of delaying a combined validity decision. Interleaving may expose independent lookup work while per-group checks constrain live values and preserve fallback behavior; the larger schedule can still lose to register pressure or code size. No speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this scalar table decoder, prior two-, three-, four-, and eight-group unrolls were all correct but slower than the recorded baseline; the four-group version was closest. This motivates testing scheduling differences rather than assuming a larger factor is faster.
memory_lessons.claim: Repeated scalar unroll measurements do not establish a speedup over baseline: means were 82.32 µs (two groups), 147.64 µs (three), 63.81 µs (four), and 81.30 µs (eight), against 55.00 µs baseline.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this four-group interleaved-lookup schedule with the controller; compare it only with compatible validated measurements.

data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed; the decoder remains scalar and serial. The bulk guard requires at least 37 remaining characters before reading 32, leaving input for the original scalar path; each group is validated before it advances the input/output pointers, so an invalid group falls back at that group. Prior two-, three-, four-, and eight-group measurements were all slower than baseline; this action contains no new validation or timing results. The controller must check short and boundary lengths, padding, random valid inputs, and Lena before timing.
transformations: Replaced the two-group bulk loop with a four-group, 32-character scalar loop guarded by 37 remaining characters to leave tail/padding work to the existing scalar decoder.
Loaded and table-decoded four independent eight-character blocks, interleaving the eight lookup positions across blocks to expose independent scalar lookup chains.
Validated and wrote each decoded block in input order, advancing pointers only after that block passes validation; retained existing bytewise fallback for invalid data, padding, and tails.
Added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-length specialization, or changes outside src/candidate.cpp.
